headline: Every major back above its 200-day line while bitcoin whales send coin to exchanges: a market rallying and hedging at the same time
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because today it is unusually clean: all seven majors are green on the day, and five of seven, bitcoin, ether, solana, XRP and BNB, sit above their 200-day averages with golden crosses confirmed. Doge and Cardano are the holdouts, still under their 200-day lines despite firm daily gains of 3.4% and 5.2%. That is a market where the trend-following crowd has the wind at its back on most names, but not all of them, and the laggards are worth remembering when the mood turns extrapolative.

Momentum tells a more interesting story than the price action alone. RSI readings cluster in the high 50s to low 60s across the board (BTC 60.6, ETH 62.8, XRP 62.7), which is firm without being stretched, room left before anyone calls it overbought. But every single asset shows MACD below signal. That is a real divergence: price pushing higher (XRP up 9.8% on the day, up 35.7% on the month) while the momentum oscillator used for trend-confirmation is still rolling over from a prior peak. It does not invalidate the move, but it means the rally is running ahead of its own momentum confirmation, not the other way around.

Positioning adds texture. Funding is positive but unremarkable across the board, BTC at 7.0% annualized, ETH barely paying at 0.9%, XRP and SOL both near 11%. Nobody is paying a fortune to stay long, so this isn't a crowded, expensive trade by the funding measure alone. But the long/short account ratios tell a different story: XRP's ratio is 2.22, doge's is 4.36, both signaling a retail crowd heavily tilted long relative to shorts. Liquidations back that read up: BTC saw $1.3M in short liquidations against zero longs in the last hour, XRP $1.46M in shorts wiped against just $57K in longs. Shorts are getting squeezed, not longs, which is consistent with a market grinding upward and punishing anyone betting against it.

Flows are where the picture gets genuinely mixed. Bitcoin's spot ETF printed an outflow of $13.2M on 11 Sep, and the five-session net is a larger outflow of $288.1M, four straight days in the same direction. That's a traditional-finance bid quietly stepping back even as price rallies 3.1% on the day. Ether ETFs show the opposite: $216.4M inflow on the same date, $222.8M net over five sessions, though same_direction_days of just 1 means call that a fresh turn, not an entrenched trend yet. Layer on the whale data and the tension deepens: over the trailing 72 hours, $173.4M in bitcoin net value moved onto exchanges, and the week ending Sep 14 shows $725M onto exchanges, reversing the prior week's $267M that moved off. Coin moving toward exchanges alongside a strong price day is the kind of thing that reads either as profit-taking supply or as dry powder positioning for use, the data doesn't tell you which, only that it's happening.

Sentiment closes the loop and adds one more contradiction. The Fear & Greed gauge sits at 57, labeled Greed, mid-pack in its own 30-day range of 31 to 74. Nothing frothy there. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.25% over 30 days to $310B, no dramatic surge of fresh dry powder. So you have a crowd that isn't especially euphoric, a bitcoin ETF quietly leaking money, whale coin heading toward exchanges, and yet price and short-side liquidations both say the tape is grinding higher with shorts getting run over. Worth watching from here: whether the bitcoin ETF's four-day outflow streak breaks or extends, whether MACD crosses back above signal to confirm what price is already doing, and whether next week's whale flow flips back off-exchange the way it did for the week ending Sep 07.
